title: Network Theory Numericals 14: RC and RL Transients

scenes.narration: Welcome back. Today we solve transient problems: a capacitor discharging, an inductor's current building up, and a capacitor that starts already charged, using the general formula. Remember the three things you always need: the initial value, the final value and the time constant.
scenes.title: RC & RL TRANSIENTS
scenes.subtitle: Solved problems, step by step

scenes.title: Problem 1 · Capacitor discharge
given: Discharges through R = 100 kΩ at t = 0
scenes.ask:
τ, v after 2 s, time to fall
to 10 V, initial energy
scenes.narration: Problem one. A ten microfarad capacitor charged to one hundred volts is discharged through a one hundred kilo-ohm resistor when the switch closes. Find the time constant, the voltage after two seconds, the time to fall to ten volts, and the energy stored at the start.

scenes.title: Problem 1 · Capacitor discharge
scenes.narration: Step one: tau equals R C, one hundred thousand times ten times ten to the minus six, one second. Step two: a discharging capacitor follows v equals V zero times e to the minus t over tau. At two seconds: one hundred times e to the minus two, thirteen point five three volts.

scenes.title: Problem 1 · Capacitor discharge
scenes.narration: Step three: to find when it reaches ten volts, set ten equals one hundred e to the minus t. Then e to the minus t is zero point one, and t is the natural log of ten, two point three zero three seconds. Step four: the initial energy is one half C V squared, half times ten to the minus five times ten thousand, zero point zero five joules.

scenes.title: Problem 2 · RL current build-up
given: V = 24 V, R = 8 Ω, L = 4 H
Switch closed at t = 0, no initial current
scenes.ask:
τ, final current,
i at 0.5 s and 1 s
scenes.narration: Problem two. A twenty four volt source is switched onto an eight ohm resistor in series with a four henry inductor. Find the time constant, the final current, and the current after zero point five and one second.

scenes.title: Problem 2 · RL current build-up
scenes.narration: Step one: for an RL circuit, tau equals L over R, four over eight, zero point five seconds. Step two: in the final state, the inductor acts like a wire, so the current is twenty four over eight, three amperes. Step three: the current rises as three times one minus e to the minus t over zero point five, which is e to the minus two t.

scenes.title: Problem 2 · RL current build-up
scenes.narration: At zero point five seconds, one time constant: three times zero point six three two, one point nine amperes. At one second, two time constants: three times zero point eight six five, two point five nine amperes. And at t equals zero, the current is zero, because an inductor's current cannot jump. Remember: tau equals L over R, not R times L.

scenes.title: Problem 3 · Starting from a charged capacitor
given: 12 V source, R = 2 kΩ, C = 500 µF
Capacitor already at 4 V before t = 0
scenes.ask:
v(t), v at 1 s,
time to reach 10 V
scenes.narration: Problem three. A five hundred microfarad capacitor already charged to four volts is connected through two kilo-ohms to a twelve volt source. Find v of t, the voltage after one second, and when it reaches ten volts.

scenes.title: Problem 3 · Starting from a charged capacitor
scenes.narration: Step one: find the three values. The initial voltage is four volts, because a capacitor's voltage cannot jump. The final voltage is twelve volts, because in the end the capacitor acts like an open circuit and no current flows. Tau is two thousand times five hundred micro, one second. Step two: the general formula, v equals final plus initial minus final times e to the minus t over tau: twelve plus four minus twelve, e to the minus t, which is twelve minus eight e to the minus t.

scenes.title: Problem 3 · Starting from a charged capacitor
scenes.narration: Step three: at one second, twelve minus eight times zero point three six eight, nine point zero six volts. Step four: set twelve minus eight e to the minus t equal to ten. Then e to the minus t is a quarter, so t is the natural log of four, one point three nine seconds. The classic mistake is to use the plain charging formula, which assumes the capacitor starts at zero.

Exam tips. Always find the initial value, the final value and the time constant first. Capacitor voltage and inductor current never jump. Tau is R C for capacitors and L over R for inductors. Use the general formula for any starting value, and use the natural log to solve for time.
